newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt tighter amid adversity elsewhere.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt tighter amid adversity elsewhere.

text.p: U.S. corporate bonds bucked the negative trends seen in skittish government bond and equities markets on Thursday as spreads tightened across all sectors, dealers said.
High-yield credits also outperformed the government debt market with prices there seen flat to marginally higher.

Back in investment grades, cable sector debt was turning out to the darling of the market this week with Viacom Inc shaving 10 to 15 basis points off its long yield spreads. News Corp debt, which had largely lagged the upmove, garnered best interest on Thursday and tightened three to five basis points.

News Corp's bid emerged after news that Cablevision Systems Corp reiterated its right to first refusal to buy a 50 percent stake in the Madison Square Garden properties, analysts said, adding that those are the same properties eyed by News Corp and a unit of Tele-Communications Inc.
Bondholders rejoiced as it appeared News Corp would be less likely to deplete cash reserves, analysts said.

Separately, traders said paper from Tele-Communications Inc and Time Warner Inc held unchanged from yesterday's close, but the consensus called for further gains. Viacom paper forged gains as it has every day this week, they added.
Dealers said market tone was very positive as long U.S. Treasuries and the stock market sold off.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 92.75 points to the backside of the 7000 level, led by a sharp selloff in technology stocks. U.S. Treasuries, meanwhile, fell following unfriendly economic news including a jump in the Philadelphia Fed's index of manufacturing activity from 11.3 to 17.4.

Buying in longer paper outpaced the intermediate part of the curve, corporate traders said, as investors capitalize on a relatively steep curve. Still, demand was considered strong throughout the curve by most accounts.

The new issue market was limited to a $200 million issue of 10-year A2/single-A first mortgage bonds from Virginia Electric & Power Co via J.P. Morgan Securities. The notes were priced as 6-3/4s to yield 6.929 percent or 60 basis points over the curve.
In the private placement market, Sakura Bank's Sakura Capital Funding Ltd priced $1.0 billion in two-tranche Baa2/BBB subordinated perpetual debt via Merrill Lynch & Co.

A $400 million tranche was priced at par to yield 7.32 percent or 120 basis points over the five-year Treasury. Another $600 million floating-rate par notes were priced at the three-month LIBOR for a spread of 95 basis points over five year Treasuries.

Street talk also stirred around the $1.25 billion global bond offering from Ford Motor Credit Corp. The deal, expected to be priced on Friday at 38 to 39 basis points over via joint leads Goldman, Sachs & Co and Merrill Lynch, was increased in size from $1.0 billion on Thursday.
Oracle Corp's $300 million seven- and 10-year notes of Wednesday closed at issued spreads of 52 and 62 basis points over, respectively. The 10-years were tighter at mid-session.
In the high-yield market, traders said demand was powerful for telecom and broadcasting names in particular. Globalstar and TCI Satellite Entertainment's new issues were quoted flat at the close.
The 30-year T-bond closed off 31/32 to yield 6.65 percent.
